1.o: After the inscription (ver. 1, 2) we have, I. The charge given to Timothy, ver. 3, 4. II. The true end of the law (ver. 5-11), where he shows that it is entirely agreeable to the gospel. III. He mentions his own call to be an apostle, for which he expresses his thankfulness, ver. 12-16. IV. His doxology, ver. 17. V. A renewal of the charge to Timothy, ver. 18. And of Hymenæus and Alexander, ver. 19, 20.
1.i: 1 Timothy 1 to 3 are Paul's advice to a younger pastor about teaching, prayer and leadership.
1.p: Lord, bless those who lead, and give leaders wisdom. Make Your church a household of truth and love. Amen.
1.l: Pray for someone in charge, such as a teacher, a mayor or a leader, and say their name out loud.
q: Paul told Timothy to pray even for rulers who persecuted Christians. Who is hard for you to pray for?

2.o: In this chapter Paul treats, I. Of prayer, with many reasons for it, ver. 1-8. II. Of women's apparel, ver. 9, 10. III. Of their subjection, with the reasons of it, ver. 11-14. IV. A promise given for their encouragement in child-bearing, ver. 15.
2.i: 1 Timothy 1 to 3 are Paul's advice to a younger pastor about teaching, prayer and leadership.
2.p: Lord, bless those who lead, and give leaders wisdom. Make Your church a household of truth and love. Amen.
2.l: Pray for someone in charge, such as a teacher, a mayor or a leader, and say their name out loud.
q: Paul told Timothy to pray even for rulers who persecuted Christians. Who is hard for you to pray for?

3.o: In this chapter our apostle treats of church-officers. He specifies, I. The qualifications of a person to be admitted to the office of a bishop, ver. 1-7. II. The qualifications of deacons (ver. 8-10), and of their wives (ver. 11), again of the deacons, ver. 12, 13. III. The reasons of his writing to Timothy, whereupon he speaks of the church and the foundation-truth professed therein, ver. 14, to the end.
3.i: 1 Timothy 1 to 3 are Paul's advice to a younger pastor about teaching, prayer and leadership.
3.p: Lord, bless those who lead, and give leaders wisdom. Make Your church a household of truth and love. Amen.
3.l: Pray for someone in charge, such as a teacher, a mayor or a leader, and say their name out loud.
q: Paul told Timothy to pray even for rulers who persecuted Christians. Who is hard for you to pray for?

4.o: Paul here foretels, I. A dreadful apostasy, ver. 1-3. II. He treats of Christian liberty, ver. 4, 5. III. He gives Timothy divers directions with respect to himself, his doctrine, and the people under his care, ver. 6, to the end.
4.i: 1 Timothy 4 to 6 are Paul's practical advice to a young leader: set an example, care for people, and be content.
4.p: Lord, make us examples in word and in life. Give us contentment and open hands. Amen.
4.l: Do something kind for a person older than you, and something kind for a person younger than you.
q: The laying on of hands passes on authority. Who is passing something on to you, and to whom are you passing it?

5.o: Here the apostle, I. Directs Timothy how to reprove, ver. 1, 2. II. Adverts to widows, both elder and younger, ver. 3-16. III. To elders, ver. 17-19. IV. Treats of public reproof, ver. 20. V. Gives a solemn charge concerning ordination, ver. 21, 22. VI. Refers to his health (ver. 23), and states men's sins to be very different in their effects, ver. 24, 25.
5.i: 1 Timothy 4 to 6 are Paul's practical advice to a young leader: set an example, care for people, and be content.
5.p: Lord, make us examples in word and in life. Give us contentment and open hands. Amen.
5.l: Do something kind for a person older than you, and something kind for a person younger than you.
q: The laying on of hands passes on authority. Who is passing something on to you, and to whom are you passing it?

6.o: I. He treats of the duty of servants, ver. 1, 2. II. Of false teachers, ver. 3-5. III. Of godliness and covetousness, ver. 6-10. IV. What Timothy was to flee, and what to follow, ver. 11, 12. V. A solemn charge, ver. 13-16. VI. A charge for the rich, ver. 17-19. And lastly, a charge to Timothy, ver. 20, 21.
6.i: 1 Timothy 4 to 6 are Paul's practical advice to a young leader: set an example, care for people, and be content.
6.p: Lord, make us examples in word and in life. Give us contentment and open hands. Amen.
6.l: Do something kind for a person older than you, and something kind for a person younger than you.
